overview: Convergent mixed methods study: a quantitative strand on housing outcomes and hospital use of inpatients referred to housing first in 2024 and 2025, and a qualitative strand of peer-led interviews, integrated in a joint display.
population: Quantitative: inpatients experiencing homelessness referred from the hospital in 2024 and 2025 (about 260), and eligible non-referred inpatients in the same years matched two to one on prior emergency use, age and diagnosis group. Qualitative: 12 to 15 referred people, 10 social workers and 8 housing-first staff.
exposure: Referral to housing first by hospital social work during the index admission.
procedures: Hospital data extracted for both groups; tenancy outcomes linked by the provider's named custodian after the agreement is signed; a peer researcher and the team's research social worker conduct interviews with layered consent and payment; a community advisory group of people with lived experience meets every two months.

outcomes.name: Housed within six months (quantitative strand)
outcomes.measure: Tenancy start within six months of the referral date, from provider records
outcomes.why: The outcome the referral exists for.

outcomes.name: What helps or blocks referral (qualitative strand)
outcomes.measure: Themes from interviews with referred people and staff, with a joint display against referral failure points

outcomes.name: Emergency department visits in 12 months
outcomes.measure: Visits per person-year, referred against matched eligible non-referred inpatients, with planned outpatient attendance as a negative control
outcomes.why: Hospital use the executive asked about (claim c1).

outcomes.name: Referral completeness
outcomes.measure: Proportion of referrals with identity documents, income details and a named contact recorded

outcomes.name: Social work time per referral
outcomes.measure: Minutes recorded by social workers for a sample of referrals
outcomes.why: A pathway that costs too much time will not last.

feasibility: About 260 referred and 520 comparison inpatients from existing data; 200 peer researcher hours cover about 30 interviews with transcription support.
biasMitigation: Eligibility defined identically for both groups
Matching on prior emergency use with propensity weights
Negative control outcome for residual confounding
Peer-led interviews to reduce social desirability

biasFlags.label: Confounding by engagement
biasFlags.note: Handled by matching, weighting and a negative control; not removed.

biasFlags.label: Loss to contact among referred people
biasFlags.note: Interview sample may over-represent people who were housed.

flags: One primary outcome per strand, by design
parsimony.simplestPath: Two strands, one primary outcome each, one joint display.

theoreticalFramework: Convergent mixed methods design; no further framework.
summary: Two strands with one primary outcome each, a secondary comparison of emergency use, and process and balancing measures.
